issues.note: The rock arch r0 (and copies r3, r6) is a slab peaking at about 6 px. The crest along the lit upper edge should reach about 18-20 px, with the band averaging about 12 px (analysis: 12.5 mean, 21.5 max), and slope down to the ground at the arch's outer ends.

The cross-section is a flat-topped plate with vertical sides and a thin lip. It should be a rounded, faceted rock mound, roughly a half-cylinder along the arch: highest along the highlighted crest, sloping down to the outer edge, and dropping into the undercut on the inner (concave) side. The crest highlight and side shading should then come from the form.

The dark shadowed band under the inside of each arch (the cave opening) is only painted on a flat surface. It should be real geometry: the inner face recessed back about 6-10 px under the crest as an overhang (or a through-opening), so the shadow falls into it.

A saw-tooth fringe of 1-2 px triangular spikes from the displacement noise runs along the inner and lower edges, and roughens the top edge in panel 2. Remove the fine noise at the edges, keep the outline smooth and following the sprite, and turn the edge into the sloped flank of the mound.

The sprite's large boulder facets, separated by dark cracks along the top of each arch, have no matching relief; the surface noise is random. Replace the noise with a few large rounded lobes, each raised 2-4 px, following the facets, and cut the crack lines about 1-2 px deep.
Faint lines cross the rock at piece boundaries from the game camera (e.g. a vertical line through the top arch). Weld the vertices or match the normals across pieces so the joins disappear.

Lit from above, the rock reads greyer and duller than the sprite's warm tan, even though the flat colours match (dE 2.3). Check the material's specular/roughness (and the base tint) so the lit top view keeps the sprite's warm tan.

The small rock chunks r1/r2 (and their copies r4/r5, r7/r8) at the arch ends are 1.3-1.6 px plates. The analysis puts r1 at about 5 px, so make them small rounded boulders of about that height, blending into the arch's sloping ends.

issues.note: The twin blue columns (r19 left, r3 right, with the grid tops r1/r4) top out at about 6-7 px, only about 4 px above the deck. In the sprite they're about 20 px wide round tubes with a highlight stripe; raise them to about 15-20 px (at least a full half-cylinder standing about 10 px above the deck).

The blue ring r2 is a squashed torus whose tube stands about 3.5 px above the deck (top at about 6 px). The sprite's ring tube is about 12 px wide with strong top highlights; give it a near-circular section, about 10-12 px tall.

The column bodies are rounded-edge slabs with flat lids. Make them cylinders lying along the screen's vertical axis, so the sprite's highlight stripe and dark right edge come from the lighting, with the grid plates r1/r4 following the curved top.

The side gun stacks (r17/r18, r37/r38, r32/r33, r44 and their mirrors) are ball-and-capsule chains about 6-7 px tall. The sprite shows straight stacks of cylinder segments of stepped width, about 10 px wide at the base; rebuild them as stacked cylinders about 10-13 px tall.
There is red along both sides of each gun stack in the diff: the model's segments are narrower than the sprite's (coverage about 0.6-0.7). Widen each segment to its sprite width.

The main deck r42 is a 2-3 px slab. The sprite's lit-edge stripes on the wings say the plates are bevelled and stacked; make it about 5-6 px thick at the centre, bevelling down to about 2 px at the purple wing tips.

The dark strip right of the ring and down the right side (r41, near-black in the sprite, dE 44.5) is modelled as light grey striped deck. Make it a dark channel cut 2-3 px into the deck, in the sprite's shadow colour.

The lamps r25/r27 are flat light cornflower blue (dE 38-48). The sprite's are deep saturated electric blue with a near-white cyan core, so use an emissive bright blue with a lighter centre. The columns and ring should also shift from flat steel-blue toward the sprite's navy with cyan highlights.

The outer gun stacks (r17/r37, r32 and their mirrors) are centred near deck level, so their lower balls hang about 1-1.5 px below the deck's underside (also visible in panel 5). Raise them so nothing goes below 0 px.
Inside the ring, the dark cavity r53/r57 is only about 2 px below the hull. The sprite shows a deep dark well; cut it about 4-6 px below the hull top.
The ribbed grille r35 on the right column shows as a row of separate bumps floating about 1 px above the column top. Seat the ribs into the column surface so they follow its curve.
The sprite's 1-2 px dark outline along the outer purple wing edges (r55/r56) is missed (red rim in the diff). Extend the wing edges about 1 px with a dark bevel.

issues.note: The glass dome r0 (and r56 on the lower copy) is a low lens, crowning at about 4-6 px over a footprint about 55 px across. It should be an egg-shaped dome about 25 px tall (at least half its width; Opus suggested 25-30, Fable 20-24), taller toward the sprite's top. It should meet the cobbles at the sprite's purple rim and keep the specular highlight upper-left.

The city towers (r1, r2, r20 and the small tower regions r3-r16; r57-r76 on the lower copy) are flat tiles 3-8 px tall lying like a mosaic. They should be upright rectangular prisms with vertical facades: the tall centre towers about 20-24 px, the ring of smaller ones 10-16 px, stepping down toward the dome edge.

The towers poke through the glass: their tops reach about 8 px while the dome crown is about 4-6 px, so in panels 7-9 the city sits on top of a lens instead of inside a bubble. Every tower must sit fully inside the shell. Raise the dome to about 25 px and keep the tallest tower a few px below it.

From above the glass reads grey-silver, with purple only at the rim. The sprite's glass is deep violet with a lilac highlight and a darker purple rim. Darken and saturate the glass material toward violet, keep it translucent so the towers show through, and let lighting make the highlight.

In the sprite they're dark blue-teal, with pale cyan lit faces on their upper-left sides (r3, r4, r9, r10) and scattered cyan/white window pixels. Use a dark teal material, lighten the upper-left faces, and add emissive or shallow inset window rows.
The cobble ground plates are dull grey-brown. The sprite's cobbles are warm orange-brown with dark gaps, so warm the plate colour toward the sprite's.

On the lower-right the dome rim flattens into a purple ledge or skirt instead of curving down into the ground. Keep the shell's curve continuous all the way to the cobbles (it should follow from rebuilding the dome).

reasons.cohesion: The seam metrics are clean (mean dz 0.005 px, max 0.24 px, none over 1 px; the 78 gap samples aren't visible), and the ground plates and the overlapping second tile meet without steps. The sprite's pale highlight blob (about 3x3 px, upper-left) is modelled as a separate ball, about 5 px across, rising about 1.5 px above the body. It reads as a wart in panels 7-9. It's a specular highlight: delete the knob, and let the taller round body's lighting plus a lighter tint there produce it.

The model is about 1 px inside the sprite's outline all round (solid red ring, 42 px missed, 0 extra). Grow the body's radius by about 1 px, to about 7.5 px (the sprite's 14 x 15 px circle), so the dark rim pixels become its shadowed edge.

The pale swirl crescent (lower-right) is a thin separate fin that stands off the body in panel 5, with a deep dark groove beside it. Keep the swirl, since it's a real marking in the sprite's interior, but make it flush: a pale colour band or a rib at most about 0.5 px proud following the sphere's curvature, with the groove as a dark tint or a recess under 0.5 px deep.

The body is a uniform, slightly dark and grey mid steel-blue (dE 14.5). The sprite has a near-white ice-blue highlight upper-left, a mid steel blue and a dark navy rim. Lighten and saturate the base a little, add the lighter blue upper-left, and darken toward the rim.

newshn-125-current.notes: First, rebuild r0 as a near-spherical orb about 15 px across and 8-12 px tall, instead of a 4 px bun that's 1 px too small. reasons.detail: The model has a dark curved groove through the centre and a pale raised crescent lower-right, which match the sprite's dark central curve and pale lower-right crescent. These markings sit inside the ball, not on its rim, so they read as a real swirl pattern, not just sphere shading. But the knob is an invented detail (a misread highlight), and the crescent strip floats off the surface. Opus gave 3 (swirl present) and Fable 2 (all three features are shading mistaken for shape); I scored 2 because the swirl is a valid marking but the most visible 'detail' is wrong.
reasons.game: From the game camera (panel 9) it reads as a blue orb with a bump and a swirl: recognisably the blue swirl orb, by outline, colour and marking. The knob changes the read, and the low body makes it look more like a puck than a ball. Fable gave 2; I went with 3 because it's still clearly the sprite's enemy.
reasons.overall: The body needs to become one smooth, near-spherical orb about 1 px wider (about 15 px across) and 8-12 px tall, with the highlight coming from the material and lighting, not a bump. The swirl can stay as a flush colour band or very shallow relief. As it stands it misreads the sprite's highlight as shape and is half height, so 2.
reasons.profile: The body is rounded but squashed into a bun (h/w about 0.29 for the body alone), not a sphere or tall dome. The sprite's upper-left specular highlight has been modelled as a separate ball, about 5 px across, sitting on the dome, which reads as a wart in panels 7-9. The swirl crescent is a thin separate strip that stands off the surface in panel 5 instead of following the curvature. Round thing modelled flat, with a lump, so 2.
reasons.silhouette: The outline is round like the sprite but about 1 px small all round: panel 4 shows a solid red ring (IoU 0.781, 42 px missed, 0 extra). The sprite's dark rim pixels are the ball's shadowed edge, so they belong to the shape. The base colour is the right steel-blue family (dE 14.5), but the model is a uniform, slightly dark mid-blue. It lacks the sprite's pale ice-blue highlight upper-left and its dark navy rim, and the separate knob and crescent catch light where the sprite is smooth. Target: about 15 px across, one steel-blue material shaded lighter upper-left and darker at the rim.
reasons.volume: On the panel 5/6 rulers the main body (r0) rises only about 3.5-4 px at its centre over a diameter of about 14 px. A separate knob reaches 5.4 px (max_height 5.41; the analysis estimates 8.4 px max). The sprite shades it as a ball (dark rim all round, highlight upper-left), so it should be at least a hemisphere about 7.5 px tall, ideally near-spherical at 10-12 px. The body is about half its proper height, so 2.

issues.note: r0, the lower-right shadow: in the game view the bottom third of the ball (about 4-5 px of its 15) is near-black, and from above (panel 2) the navy rim is about 2 px wide, where the sprite's dark rim is a 1 px band. issues.note: r0, the orb body: a lens ~3 px thick (top ~1.3 px), with the frame at ~2 px and the pyramid peaking at 3.3 px, on a ~16.5 px wide body. The sprite's even fall-off from a bright centre to a dark rim says it's a sphere, so rebuild it as a sphere or a dome at least half as tall as it is wide: top ~8-9 px above the midplane (the analysis infers 9.7).

The centre is a hard four-sided pyramid in a square tray. The sprite's centre is a soft round highlight on a curved surface, so drop the pyramid and the tray and let the dome's apex carry the bright centre (a small faceted cap ~0.5 px proud is fine if you want the sparkle).

The diamond: a hard raised frame (~2 px) with a black moat, reaching almost to the rim, so it reads as a badge. In the sprite it's a pattern of dark-blue pixels on the orb's surface. Make it a shallow groove or low ridge (~0.5-1 px) that follows the sphere's curvature, in mid-dark blue, not black.
The radius is ~1-1.5 px short all round (a solid red ring; 68 of 276 px missed, none extra). Grow the body so its edge, including the sprite's dark navy rim pixels, matches the sprite's circle.

The outer disc is a uniform dull grey-blue (dE 13.7). The sprite's body is a brighter steel blue, darkening to navy at the rim. Raise the saturation and brightness toward the sprite's mid-blue, with a darker rim.

Between the diamond and the rim, the sprite has pale blue and white speckles forming light diagonal spokes from the diamond's corners out to the rim, with bright spots at the lower-right. The model's surface there is plain. Add them as pale facets or faint ~0.3 px ridges (or vertex colour) to bring back the sparkle.

reasons.detail: The main motif is present: the diamond inscribed in the circle, the dark inner diamond, and the bright centre point (as a pyramid). But the diamond is a hard raised frame with a black moat that dominates the top view, where the sprite draws it as a softer dark-blue pattern on the orb. The pale blue and white speckles between the diamond and the rim, which form light diagonal spokes from the diamond corners (with bright spots at the lower-right), are missing. Both gave 3.
reasons.game: From the game camera (panel 9) it reads as a blue gem in a square setting on a coaster, not the glossy faceted orb of the sprite. The colours and motif make it recognisable, but the square frame is the strongest feature and there's no volume or sparkle. Opus gave 2 and Fable 3; I took 2 because the shape reads as a different object (a badge).
reasons.overall: Poor: the motif and colour family are right, but the volume is almost entirely missing (3.3 px max where ~9 is implied), and the hard square frame and pyramid turn an orb into a badge. Both gave 2. It needs rebuilding as a sphere or tall dome, with the diamond as a shallow pattern on its surface.
reasons.profile: The orb is modelled as a thin lens, then a flat square frame (a tray) and a hard four-sided pyramid on top (panel 7), so a round thing has been made flat and boxy. reasons.silhouette: The round outline, the diamond motif and the bright centre are in the right place (panel 3). Colours are in the right blue family (dE 13.7), but the disc is a uniform dull grey-blue, missing the sprite's brighter steel blue and its pale blue and white speckles. Both gave 3.

issues.note: The dark base plate used to fill the silhouette (panel 5: a flat slab 0 to -1 px spanning the whole footprint) shows in the game view as a flat dark diamond skirt around the tail exhaust r1 and as a lip in front of the nose tip. Trim the plate so it extends no more than about 0.5 px beyond the parts above it (or bevel its edge down at 45 degrees), and widen the tail cylinder's base to meet it so no flat flange shows.

The sprite's near-white highlight pixels along the right pod's inner edge (rows 10-18) and at both strut/pod junctions (row 17-18) are absent; the model's right pod is uniform dark grey there (brightest yellow in the diff). Add a lit raised bevel or lighter vertex colour along the right pod's inner rim and a 1 px bright cap at each strut/pod junction.

The cockpit is a full sphere about 4 px across whose top is at 8.3 px over a 4.5 px hull, so it perches 3.5-4 px proud and reads as a ball in the game view. The sprite's light cluster under the canopy band is a 3 x 2 px patch; make it a low dome about 4 px wide and 2 px proud of the hull, sunk into the segment.

The step lines between hull segments (sprite rows 9, 12-13 and 16, drawn black 1 px) are modelled as lit chamfers that show as light-grey rings in the top view. Make each step a 0.5 px dark undercut (the upper segment overhanging the lower) so the lines read dark from above as in the sprite.

The main hull segment tops out at about 4-4.5 px for an 8 px wide body, a half-round. The sprite's strong centre stripe with dark flanks suggests a fuller section; raising the main and cockpit segments about 1 px (to 5.5 px, keeping the nose taper) would match better. Polish only.

ship-gencore-phoenix-fixed.notes: 1) Trim or bevel the base plate so it does not show as a flat dark skirt around the tail exhaust r1 and in front of the nose in the game view. 2) Add the sprite's bright highlights along the right pod's inner edge and at the strut/pod junctions (the remaining colour error). 3) Lower the cockpit from a perched 4 px ball (top 8.3 px) to a 2 px proud dome sunk into the segment. 4) Turn the lit chamfers between hull segments into dark 0.5 px undercuts so the step lines read dark from above. 5) Optionally raise the main hull about 1 px to 5.5 px.

reasons.detail: Present in relief: the four hull segments, the centre ridge highlight on the nose and aft segments, the cockpit dome, the dark notch at the ridge/tail junction (the sprite's rear port), the nacelle inner rims, the tail nozzle cap, and the step lines between segments. Missing: the near-white highlight pixels along the right pod's inner edge and at both strut/pod junctions (bright yellow in panel 4), and the sprite's dark 1 px step lines read as light bevel rings in the top view instead of dark grooves. Most details there; 4.
reasons.game: From the game camera (panel 9) it reads as the sprite in 3D: dark charcoal, segmented tapering hull with a bright dome, twin blade nacelles on cylinder struts, blunt exhaust. Two small tells: the dome is a bright perched ball larger than the sprite's light cluster, and the base plate shows as a flat dark diamond skirt around the tail exhaust and a dark lip in front of the nose. 4.
reasons.overall: A different model in kind from the previous sheet: exact outline, right colour, plausible heights and profiles, the main details in relief, and it reads as the sprite from the game camera. What remains is polish: the perched dome, the visible base-plate skirt at the tail and nose, the missing pod highlights, and the step lines as lit bevels instead of dark grooves. Good; 4.
reasons.profile: The hull is round in the front elevation (panel 6: about 7 px wide, 4.5 px tall above the plane, rounded top), built as stacked segments with a tapering stepped nose; the tail r1 is a blunt cylinder about 4 px wide; the cockpit is a sphere about 4 px across; the struts are cylinders and the nacelles are faceted blades with a raised inner rim, matching the sprite's irregular pods. The segment steps are lit chamfers rather than dark cuts, and the dome is a full ball rather than a low dome. Round parts round, tapers taper; 4.
reasons.silhouette: IoU 1.0 (0 px missed, 0 px extra) on the 22 x 25 px footprint, up from 0.694: the model now covers the sprite's dark edge everywhere, done with a thin dark base plate about 1 px thick under the parts (visible in panel 5 as a slab from 0 to -1 px running the full length). Colour dE 6.5 (was 18.0): the olive-green cast is gone and the hull is the sprite's neutral dark charcoal; panel 4 is mostly dim yellow with a few brighter spots on the right nacelle's inner edge (fx 0.75, fy 0.7) where the sprite has near-white highlight pixels the model lacks, and on the nose tip. Top view matches closely; 4.
reasons.volume: max_height 8.33 px (was 3.61), h/w 0.49. In the side elevation the main hull top is at about 4-4.5 px for an 8 px wide body (half-round), stepping down through 3 px and 2 px to the 2 px wide nose tip; the cockpit dome rises to 8.3 px; the tail exhaust cylinder is about 3 px tall; the nacelles stand about 3 px for 3 px wide. Everything is now in the right range for its width; the main hull could be another 1 px taller for its strong centre highlight. 4.

issues.note: The outline match comes from a flat dark plate in the sprite's full silhouette under the model: about 0.8 px thick (0.2 to 1.0 px in panels 5 and 6), it sticks out about 1 px past the wings, the nose tip and the tail as a flat flange, visible under the wingtips and tail in panels 7-8 and as a dark bar the whole length of the ship in panel 5. Remove it and instead extend the wing plates 1 px at the tips and leading edges, the nose cone 2 px and the tail 1 px (about a 10% scale) so the real parts cover the outline; if a dark edge is wanted, make it a dark bevel on those parts, not a separate slab.

The hull r0 is now a neutral grey (green cast gone) but still too dark: dE 17.6, panel 4 yellow over the whole body. The sprite's hull is a light mid grey with near-white highlights on the nose, the centre rib and the wing leading edges. Lighten the base grey about 20-25% and brighten the rib and leading-edge strip materials.

The pods r2/r3 are the right size now (2 x 3 px, coverage 1.0) but have gone a dark maroon: dE 38.8 and 47.2, up from 21.2/16.5. The sprite's pods are the same bright red as the tail nozzle (r4 now dE 8.0); give the pods the nozzle's material.

Because the backing plate runs under the nose, the nose cone in side view is a light tapering cone on top (1 to 2.9 px) and a flat dark slab below (0.2 to 1 px) ending in a flat tip. Once the plate is gone the cone should taper to a point on all sides, about 5 px in diameter at the ring tapering to 0 over about 7 px.

The wing leading-edge strip and groove are present but shallow (about 0.3 px of relief) so they read only from above; the sprite's lighter inner wing panel is barely distinct. Raise the leading-edge strip to about 0.5 px proud and make the groove about 0.5 px deep so the bands show in the 3/4 views.

reasons.detail: Present: nose highlight, cockpit ring, the cockpit cut in as a dark square window with the lighter centre dot (panel 2 and 9), two red 2 x 3 px pods, three fuselage ribs with dark grooves, a lighter leading-edge strip with a dark diagonal groove on each wing, and a 4 px wide tail nozzle with a dark rim. reasons.game: From the game camera (panel 9) it reads clearly as the Stalker: spike nose, dark square cockpit with its dot, red pods, swept wings with leading-edge strips, red tail, and it is now the sprite's full size. What keeps it from a 5 is how the outline was fixed (a flat backing plate instead of extending the parts), the still-dark hull grey, and the pods going maroon. Replace the plate by extending the wings, nose and tail to the outline, lighten the grey, and restore the bright pod red.

reasons.volume: Heights are about right. reasons.volume: The hull ridge now tops out at 5.1 px (max_height_px 5.1, was 4.3) and in panel 6 the body runs from about 4.9 px down to about -1.5 px, roughly 6.3 px tall for a 6.5 px wide section, inside the 6-7 px target. In panel 5 it tapers from about 2 px at the nose tip to 4 px at the cockpit and 5 px over the rear hull. r0 actual mean 2.59 px (was 2.34). Pods about 6 px wide and 4 px tall (+2/-2), red engines about 4.5 px tall on a 3 px bar, exhaust tubes about 1.5 px across standing 1-2 px above the sunk base. Nothing reads too flat or too tall now; the pods could be a shade taller for their 6 px width but that is within tolerance.

issues.note: The leaves r2 show grey-brown patches over about a third of the blade tops: the tips of both leaves and the left leaf's upper edge (also the right leaf's outer third in panel 9). The sprite's leaves are bright green with only a 1 px dark-maroon outline; here that outline colour has been projected onto the lit blade surfaces and lights to neutral grey. Keep the blades the sprite's bright green (and darker green at the lower-right) across their whole top, and put the dark maroon only on the blades' side faces or a 1 px rim, so the leaves read green from the game camera.

Scattered yellow px in panel 4 run in a diagonal line along the edge of the yellow highlight streak and the red rim (r0 dE 9.5): the projected sprite colours are offset by about 1 px (up-left) from the sprite. Nudge the texture registration by that px, or sample the sprite at pixel centres, so the streak lands on the sprite's own px.

The body's sides below the equator are near-black with radial red/black wedges (panel 6, lower half of panel 5), because the top-down projection stretches the sprite's 1 px dark rim over the whole underside. Not visible from the game camera; if wanted, fade the side colour from the rim red to a dark red rather than black so the 3/4 views show a red carrot rather than a black-bottomed one.

ship-supercarrot-fixed.notes: Remaining problems, in fix order: (1) leaves r2: grey-brown patches on about a third of the blade tops (tips and the left leaf's upper edge) from the sprite's dark outline being projected onto the lit blades; blades should be bright green with dark maroon only on a 1 px rim or the side faces; (2) a roughly 1 px up-left misregistration of the projected body colours along the yellow streak and red rim (r0 dE 9.5), polish; (3) black underside with radial wedges on the body's sides in the elevations, cosmetic only. Outline (IoU 1.0, 0 diff px), body colour, eye, thickness, section and leaf flatness are all right.

reasons.detail: The eye r1 sits in a dark 1 px socket ring with a brown iris and pale centre spot, matching the sprite exactly (dE 0.0). The yellow highlight streak now follows the sprite's curved path from the tip down the centre-left to the eye instead of a hard 2 px stripe. The green stem knob under the body matches the sprite's stem, and nothing in the sprite is missing or invented.
reasons.game: From the game camera (panel 9) it reads as the sprite's bright red-orange carrot with the yellow streak, dark-ringed eye and flat green leaves; a player would take it for the sprite in 3D. The one thing they would notice is the leaf tips and the left leaf's outer edge going grey-brown rather than green, so the foliage looks partly dead.
reasons.overall: A clear step up to good: outline 0.987 to 1.0 with zero diff px, colour dE 37.9 to 8.3, body now the sprite's real red/orange/yellow with the curved streak, eye pixel-exact, shape and thickness unchanged and still right. Remaining work is polish: grey-brown patches on the leaf blades where the sprite's dark outline got projected onto the tops, a 1 px texture misregistration along the highlight streak, and starburst wedges on the body's sides. Fix the leaves and this is close to 5.
reasons.profile: Panel 6 shows a near-circular 13 px section with the eye dome on top; panel 5 shows the body tapering smoothly from the 13 px base to the 1 px tip with the thickest point near the base. The eye is a dome recessed in a ring. The leaves are flat lobed blades 0.5-1 px thick. The only profile blemish is cosmetic: the top-down colour projection turns the body's sides into radial red/black wedges (panel 6) and leaves the whole lower half nearly black, which is invisible from the game camera but shows in the elevations.
reasons.silhouette: Outline is now exact: silhouette_iou 1.0, 226 of 226 sprite px covered, 0 missed, 0 extra, and panel 4 has no red or blue at all. Colour went from dE 37.9 to 8.3 (r0 38.6 to 9.5, r1 15.8 to 0.0, r2 43.5 to 8.0): the body now carries the sprite's own red rim, orange fill and curved yellow streak, and the eye is pixel-exact. Panel 4 is grey over the body with scattered yellow px along the highlight streak and the leaf edges, which is a roughly 1 px misregistration of the projected colours. What keeps it off 5 is the leaves: about a third of the blade area in panel 2 shows grey-brown patches (tips of both leaves, the left leaf's upper edge) where the sprite's 1 px dark-maroon leaf outline has been laid onto the lit blade tops and renders as neutral grey instead of the sprite's bright green with a thin dark edge.
reasons.volume: The body r0 spans bbox z 1.063 units = 12.8 px for a 13 px wide base (h/w 0.998), peaking at 6.33 px above the midplane in panel 5, so it is as thick as it is wide, as the sprite's red-rim/yellow-centre shading says; the analysis agrees (actual mean 3.52 / max 6.33 px against inferred 2.98 / 5.37). The eye r1 dome tops at 6.2 px in a dark socket about 1 px deep, right for a 5 px eye. The leaves r2 sit at about 0 px (mean 0.04, max 0.91 px), flat blades, which is correct for foliage even though the analysis wants 1.6 px.

issues.note: The pod's dark intake is a flat dark L-shaped rectangle painted on the pod's upper-LEFT (about 2 px wide, 2 px tall) and visible as a flat square in panel 9. The sprite's dark pixels are at rows 6-7, cols 7-8, right of the pod's centre line. Move it to the right-of-centre position and cut it about 0.5-1 px into the dome as a shallow recess (or just let the round nose shade dark there), instead of a painted decal.

The pod is a flat greyish brown (about 6b5a3e) with no highlight gradient from above, colour_dE 17.7 (was 12.2). The sprite's pod is warm gold-brown (654920 base, 7d6538/9a8255 body, cfc39e highlight at col 6, 241408 shadow at col 8). Shift the base colour to about 7d6538 with more saturation, and make sure the round section catches the upper-left light so a bright column appears left of centre.

In the side elevation the pod's top is a flat sloped facet from +2.6 px at the rear to about +1.6 px at the nose, with a hard crease at the rear top edge. The sprite's pod is a rounded bullet: make the top a smooth curve (domed in section, rounding down toward the nose) with no planar facet or crease.

The bottom bar of the U-arm is two tan segments about 2.5 px long with a dark gap in the middle and darker end caps. The sprite's row 17 alternates light and dark every pixel (b6a279, 553c18, b6a279 ...) from col 4 to col 10. Band the bar with 1 px alternating light tan and dark brown rings (slight ribs) along its length.

The cross-struts are now about 1.5 px grey tubes at the right height, but the near-pod halves (r3, r5) are very dark, colour_dE 21-23, where the sprite draws them mid grey (5d5d5d next to the pipe, 343434 next to the pod). Lighten the strut material toward 5d5d5d.

ship-u-ship-fixed.notes: Much improved: outline now exact (IoU 1.0), pipes and arm are round tubes about 2.5-3 px in diameter, the pod is a round-sectioned 5.3 px bullet, the U-arm has its chamfers and flat bar and is tan, struts are thicker. Remaining, in order: (1) move the pod's dark intake from the upper-left to right of centre (sprite rows 6-7, cols 7-8) and cut it in as a shallow recess instead of a painted rectangle; (2) warm the pod's colour from grey-brown toward the sprite's gold-brown (dE 17.7, worse than before) and let the dome catch a highlight left of centre; (3) round off the pod's flat sloped top facet into a smooth nose; (4) band the bottom bar with 1 px alternating light/dark rings; (5) lighten the struts toward 5d5d5d.

reasons.detail: The pipe collars (sprite rows 6-7 and 11-12) are rings, the cross-struts are 1.5 px grey tubes, the chamfers and bottom bar are there and the bar is split into two segments with a dark centre gap. But the sprite's dark pixels at the pod top (rows 6-7, cols 7-8) have become a flat dark L-shaped decal on the upper-left of the pod, painted on rather than recessed and on the wrong side; the pod shows almost no light-to-dark gradient from above, so the sprite's highlight column at col 6 and dark column at col 8 are not reproduced; and the bottom bar's per-pixel light/dark alternation (row 17: b6a279/553c18/b6a279) is only loosely suggested by two tan segments with darker end caps.
reasons.game: From the game camera (panel 9) it is clearly the sprite: two grey tubes with collars and chamfered tips, a rounded brown pod slung between them on grey struts, and a tan U-frame with chamfered corners and a flat bar. Depth is believable, the tubes catch highlights and the pod reads as a solid round bullet. The one thing that jars is the flat dark square painted on the pod's upper-left, and the pod being a touch grey and flat-lit compared with the sprite's golden pod.
reasons.overall: A large step up: exact outline (IoU 0.425 to 1.0), tubes round at about 2.5-3 px, pod a round-sectioned 5.3 px bullet, arm reshaped with chamfers and recoloured tan, struts thickened. What remains is polish on the pod: warm its colour toward the sprite's gold-brown (dE 17.7 now, worse than before), move the dark intake to the right of centre and cut it in as a shallow recess instead of a painted rectangle, soften the sloped top facet into a rounded nose, and give the bottom bar its alternating bands. Good (4).
reasons.profile: In panels 5 and 6 the pipes and the U-arm show the specular streak and dark underside of round tubes, and in panels 7-9 they read as pipes, not plates. The pod's section in panel 6 is a dome about 5.5 px wide with a rounded top at +2.6 px and no painted strip or cut groove. Two small faults: in panel 5 the pod's top is a flat sloped facet running from +2.6 px at the rear down to about +1.6 px at the nose with a hard crease at the rear edge, rather than a smoothly rounded bullet nose, and the dark intake is a flat painted rectangle, not relief.
reasons.silhouette: The top view now covers the sprite exactly: silhouette_iou 1.0, 186 of 186 px, 0 missed and 0 extra, and panel 4 has no red or blue, only grey-yellow colour error along the dark rims. The pipes, collars, struts and the U-arm (straight runs, two 45-degree chamfers, flat bottom bar) sit where the sprite draws them, and the arm is now tan. Colour is the weak point: colour_dE_mean 13.9, with the pod at dE 17.7, a flat greyish brown (about 6b5a3e) where the sprite is warm gold-brown (7d6538/9a8255) with a cream cfc39e highlight column, and the pod's dark patch is a rectangle on its upper-LEFT where the sprite's dark pixels (rows 6-7, cols 7-8) are right of centre.
reasons.volume: Heights now follow each part's width. In panel 5 the side pipes span about +1.3 to -1.3 px on the ruler (about 2.5-3 px diameter, metrics actual_max 1.5) for a 1 px core plus 1 px rims; the U-arm spans about +1.2 to -1.2 px (about 2.3 px, actual_max 1.3) for its 1 px bar plus rims; the pod rises to +2.6 px (max_height_px 2.62) and drops below the panel, bbox z 0.441 units = 5.3 px, for a 5 px wide (7 with outline) round pod. The struts are about 1.5 px thick at the pipes' centre height. Nothing is a uniform extrusion any more; the previous sheet had every part at the same 4.8 px band.

issues.note: The pod crowns and the hull top between the pods now show visible facet steps: in panel 6 the outline between 3 and 4 px is jagged (several 0.2-0.3 px notches across each 6 px pod) and in panel 5 the top surface between 2.5 and 3.5 px is saw-toothed along the whole body. Last round these were smooth. Smooth-shade or subdivide the hull and pods so the pod crowns are clean round arcs and the hull top is a continuous curve, keeping the current heights (pods to about 4 px, hull to 3.5 px).

The hull colour is applied as sprite-resolution texels, so in panels 7-9 the pods and nose show square 1 px blocks of colour (visible as a checker of browns on the right pod and nose in panel 7, faintly in panel 9). From above this matches the sprite, so keep the mapping, but soften it in the 3/4 views: blend the texels (linear filtering or a slight blur) so the colour bands follow the pod curvature rather than reading as a grid.

The hull mid tone in panel 2 is still a little greyer and less saturated than panel 1's sandy gold (panel 4 shows faint yellow across the pod flanks and nose). Warm and brighten the base hull material by a small step so the lit flanks match the sprite's mid gold rather than a grey-brown.

The nose tip is bright yellow in panel 4: the cream nose keel runs all the way to the tip (panel 2, fy about 0.05-0.1) where the sprite's top two rows are dark brown outline. Stop the cream keel one or two px short of the tip and let the tip be the dark hull tone.

The groove floors are uneven in depth: panel 5 shows the cuts as notches of varying depth (0.5 to 1 px) along the body, and panel 2 still has the grooves ending about 1 px above the sprite's last dark row at the tail. Give both grooves a constant depth of about 0.7 px with a smooth floor and run them to the tail row.

ship-usp-talon-light-fighter-fixed.notes: Remaining problems, in order: (1) the pod crowns and hull top have become faceted and saw-toothed in the elevations (panel 6 jagged between 3 and 4 px, panel 5 between 2.5 and 3.5 px); smooth them without changing heights; (2) the sprite-resolution colour texels show as square blocks in the 3/4 views; blend them so they follow the pod curves; (3) the hull mid tone is still slightly grey and muted against the sprite's sandy gold; (4) the cream nose keel runs onto the dark nose tip; stop it 1-2 px short; (5) the grooves vary in depth along their length and end about 1 px short of the tail row.

reasons.detail: Canopy, both keel segments, nose steps, pods and both grooves are all modelled in relief, and the keel now carries the cream base with a white specular line along both the nose and rear segments (panel 2). The grooves are straight at the sprite's columns, about 1 px wide and dark brown with a lit edge (panel 7), ending about 1 px above the tail. Remaining: the groove floors are uneven in depth along their length (panel 5 notches of 0.5-1 px), and the hull colour comes from sprite-resolution texels that show as square blocks in the 3/4 views. Every main detail present, some polish off: 4.
reasons.game: From the game camera (panel 9) the model reads as the sprite's teardrop fighter: a dark cockpit dome, a cream crested spine, two straight dark grooves, two round shoulder pods with lighter crowns and darker flanks, and a stepped nose, now in the sprite's own browns and golds rather than the olive-tan of last round. It is slightly more muted than panel 1 and the texel blocks are faintly visible on the pods, but it looks like the sprite brought into 3D rather than a desaturated copy. Recognisable and convincing: 4.
reasons.overall: This round fixed what the previous grade asked: the palette is now the sprite's (dE 9.7 from 21.8), the keel is cream with a white line on both segments and about 2 px proud, the canopy is a dome about 1 px proud, the grooves are about 1 px wide and reach nearly to the tail, and the pod-to-hull crease is gone. Shape, heights, detail and colour are all good now. What remains is polish: faceted pod crowns and a saw-toothed hull top in the elevations, square texel blocks in the 3/4 views, a slightly muted hull tone, the cream keel spilling onto the dark nose tip, and uneven groove depth. Good: 4.
reasons.profile: Panel 6 shows the pods as round lobes and the keel as a 3 px rounded dome about 2 px proud; panel 5 shows the canopy as a dome from about 3.6 to 4.6 px sitting on the hull with no undercut, and the nose stepping down in three steps with its width. The grooves are now about 1 px wide and read as cut lines (panels 2, 7, 9). New this round: the pod crowns and hull top show visible facet steps in panel 6 (jagged outline between 3 and 4 px) and panel 5's top surface is saw-toothed between 2.5 and 3.5 px where the groove cuts and the texel colour steps meet. Right profiles, slightly rough surfaces: 4.
reasons.silhouette: Outline is still exact: silhouette_iou 1.0, 0 px missed and 0 px extra on the 266 px sprite, no red or blue in panel 4. Colour is now close: colour_dE_mean 9.7 (from 21.8), and panel 4 is grey over most of the body with yellow only along the keel highlight, the pod crowns and the nose tip, because the hull now carries the sprite's per-pixel tones (panel 2 shows the sprite's dark-brown flank columns and lighter crowns in the right places). What is left: the hull mid tone in panel 2 reads a touch greyer and less saturated than panel 1's sandy gold, and the cream keel runs right to the nose tip where the sprite's top two rows are dark outline. Exact outline, near-right palette: 4.
reasons.volume: On the panel 5 ruler the hull body runs from about -1 px to +3.5 px (bbox z 0.706 units, about 8.5 px overall) and the keel ridge tops out at 5.4 px (max_height_px 5.44, h/w 0.474, actual_mean 3.28 px against the inferred 3.92). Panel 6 shows each rear pod about 6 px wide standing from -1 px to about 4 px, about as tall as wide, with the keel about 3 px wide rising about 2 px above the hull between them (3.3 to 5.4 px), which is what a 3 px keel with a centre highlight implies. The canopy dome tops out at about 4.6 px, about 1 px above the hull; the nose steps down from about 4 px at the shoulder to about 1.5 px at the tip. Every part is close to what the sprite implies: 4.
